messages.subject: reactive expressions and actionButton
parts:
I am writing my first Shiny app and just saw this group.

In the shiny code shown below, the output is refreshed (random number changes) every time the button is clicked, irrespective of whether or not the input text changes. How can this be written so that the output is refreshed only when the button is clicked AND the input is different?

require(shiny)

ui <- shinyUI(
    navbarPage("Test",
        tabPanel("Panel1",
            fluidRow(
                column(offset=2, width=2,
                    textInput("text", label=h6("Input"), value="test123"),
                    br(),
                    actionButton("actionClick", label="Click")
                ),
                column(offset=1, width=2,
                    h6("Output"),
                    verbatimTextOutput(outputId="sessionId")
                )
            )
        )
    )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

    session <- reactive({
        input$actionClick

        isolate({
            return(input$text)
        })
    })

    output$sessionId <- renderText({paste(session(),runif(1))})
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)


FYI -- I did post this on SO when I did not know about this group [link].  I was wondering if there was a better approach than the cached variable suggested there.  Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: reactive expressions and actionButton
parts:
I don't have one I can easily dredge up, but basically you have two per session state variables (one gets set to TRUE if the button is pressed and the other if the text field changes value).  Then, in the reactive handlers for both the input field and the button, you first set the state value for your field to TRUE and then, if both are TRUE, increments a reactive value and resets the two state values to FALSE.  Finally, you have a function which is reactive on the reactive value and it generates a new random value.  In this fashion, it doesn't matter whether you press the button first or enter the text first, the random value will change after both have happened.

If that's not quite the way you want it to work (you only want a new random value when the button is pressed iff the text field had changed beforehand), you can alter the logic accordingly.

I have an example where I keep score for right/wrong clicks in an app, and the right and wrong handlers increment/decrement a common reactive value so either will update a common output accordingly.  Not your use case, but I know this sort of thing works.

Sorry to leave a probably confusing and codeless answer...
